core.title: Name the architectural layer of every feature module
core.given: A source module lives inside a feature code tree (one of the code trees to which layer rules apply)
core.when: the module exists in the tree (standing obligation; applies whenever you write, move or rename it)
core.then: The module must name its architectural layer, either by a file named for the layer or by living in a directory named for the layer, matching its actual responsibility.
prefer: Place the module in the layer that owns its responsibility, or name the file with that layer when the repository uses the filename form.
During GREEN: derive the layer from the responsibility the current behavior implements.
During GREEN: follow the nearest existing feature layout.
During GREEN: move or rename only the affected module when placement is wrong.
avoid: Choosing a layer merely to make another import rule pass.
unless: Test files and vendored/build trees are never scanned.
Source exception (verbatim): "A file carrying no layer segment is outside these rules rather than in violation of them."
core.why: A reader should know a file's role before opening it, and the layering rules need something to read. Both declaration forms are accepted because the stack's idiomatic feature layout can be nested.
evidence: The layer-naming check reports no finding for feature-tree modules (findings are verification evidence, not a precondition of the obligation).
Prove: the file's declared location or name matches its actual architectural responsibility.
Prove: the current behavioral acceptance passes.
verification: Flag a module inside the code trees to which layer rules apply whose path carries no layer directory AND whose basename is not a layer-named file; either declaration form (layer-named file or layer-named directory) satisfies the check.
Layer names are the stack's layer roles with their local names; a file named for the layer and a directory named for the layer are equally accepted, so a nested layout is compliant.

Skip test files and vendored/build trees entirely. The vendored/build trees are the stack-wide excluded list of vendored and generated trees; test files are excluded by the check's own scan scope, not by that list, and the exact classification of never-scanned paths is owned by the check.
Imports recognised as external to the project graph are not layer-checked.

Source exception (verbatim): "A file carrying no layer segment is outside these rules rather than in violation of them." Preserved unresolved: this literally conflicts with the flag condition, which targets exactly such modules, and the source does not say which rules 'these rules' means; both are kept as authored and neither side is strengthened or dropped.
Severity 2; disposition strict: the check fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

fires: Any source module inside one of the code trees to which layer rules apply — whether being written, moved, renamed or already present — is subject to the rule, whether or not a check has run.

A source module inside a code tree whose path carries no layer directory and whose basename is not a layer-named file (note: the verbatim source exception in unless literally conflicts with this case; recorded unresolved).
doesNotFire: Test files, or files in vendored/build trees.
Source files outside the code trees to which layer rules apply.
Imports of external packages, which resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked.

profileRequirements.meaning: The code trees to which layer rules apply; this is the core's scope (given, fires, and the check's flag scope).
profileRequirements.bunValue: **/features/**, **/capabilities/** (feature_tree: a path under features/ or capabilities/ — the only place this rule applies)

profileRequirements.meaning: The layer roles with their local names, i.e. the names a layer-named file or directory may carry.
profileRequirements.bunValue: domain, application, api, … (layer filenames domain.ts, application.ts, api.ts, …; a directory named for the layer equally accepted)

profileRequirements.meaning: How a module declares its layer (both accepted forms), and that a file with no layer declaration is judged by this rule's conditions.
profileRequirements.bunValue: either the filename (domain.ts, api.ts) or a directory named for the layer. Both accepted, because a nested Bun repo is idiomatic.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack-wide list of vendored and generated (vendored/build) trees that are never scanned and that the check skips. Test files are NOT entries of this list: their exclusion, and the exact classification of never-scanned paths, is owned by the check and carried in core verification and activation.
profileRequirements.bunValue: vendored/build directories are never scanned (the exact classification is deferred to the detector's test/vendored/build path classifier)

profileRequirements.meaning: How an import of an external package (outside the project graph) is recognised, for the not-layer-checked exception.
profileRequirements.bunValue: bare npm specifiers resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked

path_glob has no counterpart in the closed core fact vocabulary (role|operation|change|phase|finding|file_kind|task_term|task_has_acceptance); the scope is kept role-level in given and fires, with the concrete globs as profile data. The core's fact[0] is the merged 'source module in a code tree' file_kind fact.

file_kind: source is neutral as authored and is core fact[0]; the test/vendored/build exclusion it notes is the check's scan scope, carried in core verification and activation (test files are not entries of the stack-wide excluded list).

neutralityNotes: Four things could not be made fully neutral. (1) The closed core fact vocabulary has no path/location fact, so the feature-tree scope (path_glob) is carried by layout.code_trees and stated role-level in given/fires; the core activation fact is the merged file_kind fact. (2) The verbatim source exception 'A file carrying no layer segment...' literally conflicts with the flag condition; exactly as in the frozen rewrite, both are preserved and the conflict is recorded unresolved in core.verification — neither side strengthened nor dropped. (3) The validator id (bun_clean_architecture_detector), the term ids (layer_declaration, feature_tree), the worked example path, and the 'nested Bun repo is idiomatic' justification have no stack-neutral equivalent and remain bunOnly; severity 2 and the strict disposition stay in core.verification as per-rule facts, not profile keys. (4) roots.excluded is used only in its documented stack-wide vendored/generated-tree meaning: the test-file exclusion and the checker-owned exact classification of never-scanned paths live in core verification and activation, not in that profile list.
